subject: Collection hold: request for evidence on duplicate session charges
messages:
From: Daniel Harper <daniel@bluenova.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounting <acct@bluenova.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected late fee + collection hold on DN-4871 — duplicate session counts?

Hi Grace,

We just received invoice INV-202709-113 and a late fee plus a collection hold that has paused our ACH payment. Our finance team flagged a ~9k token overage on the invoice and suspects duplicate session attribution — the usage line shows two large bursts on 2027-09-14 03:00–03:45 UTC which we do not see in our client logs.

Key details you can use to match against your logs:
- Account: BlueNova Labs (DN-4871)
- Invoice: INV-202709-113
- Suspected window: 2027-09-14T03:00:00Z to 2027-09-14T03:45:00Z
- Example request ids (from our app trace): 9a4f2c1b, 9a4f2c1b (duplicate observed on retry), 6f7b0d55

We need the following ASAP so we can clear the hold and remit payment: a csv of request ids with timestamps for the window above, per-token counts per request id, and any evidence of server-side replays or ingestion duplicates. If this turns out to be on our side we'll take responsibility, but right now the accounting discrepancy is blocking cashflow and accrues late fees.

Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for the requested logs?

Thanks,
Daniel Harper
Head of Finance
BlueNova Labs

Subject: Re: Unexpected late fee + collection hold on DN-4871 — duplicate session counts?

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear detail. I’ve placed a temporary collection hold on INV-202709-113 while we investigate (no further late-fee escalation during the investigation window).

I’m looping in Ben (usage analytics) and Jonas (billing ops) to pull the per-request evidence. To Ben and Jonas: please pull the request_id export and per-request token counts for BlueNova for 2027-09-14 02:45:00Z through 2027-09-14 04:00:00Z and share a sample of request ids matching Daniel’s examples. If we confirm duplication on our ingestion side, we’ll calculate a retroactive credit and remove the late fee. If it’s client-side retries we’ll document it for BlueNova.

Daniel — I attached a checklist of what we’ll provide (billing_detail_export_202709.csv) and will follow up with the raw requestid list and a short technical summary by EOD tomorrow. If you can share any additional server logs or upstream retry configs it will speed triage.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachment: billing_detail_export_202709.csv (stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected late fee + collection hold on DN-4871 — duplicate session counts?

Grace / Jonas — I pulled the export you asked for. Quick summary of findings:

1) Request-id dedup: we observed ~4.8k request_ids during the window with exact duplicate request_id occurrences (~2.1k duplicates) where the same request_id appears in two ingestion batches separated by ~35–40s. Sample matched ids: 9a4f2c1b (appears twice, 2027-09-14T03:08:14.123Z and 2027-09-14T03:08:49.601Z). I’ve attached requestids_sample.txt (first 200 lines).

2) Attribution cause: trace shows client retries with identical request id and a network ACK loss combined with a backfill process that replayed cached prefixes — effectively a client retry + our re-ingest loop produced duplicates.

3) Token accounting: deduplication logic currently removes duplicates when the KV key is within the same server session, but across session boundary we didn’t correctly collapse replays for short gaps. I’ve calculated token impact for the window: 9,240 billed tokens that map to duplicate request ids.

Suggested remediation: issue a one-time credit for the 9,240 tokens (currency conversion shown in the attached spreadsheet). Also patch is ready to ensure cross-session duplicate collapse for identical request ids — I recommend we ship the patch to hosted ASAP and backfill billing correction for this account.

Attachments: requestids_sample.txt, billing_token_impact_20270914.csv

Ben Carter
Usage Analytics Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Daniel Harper <daniel@bluenova.com>
Date: 2027-10-01T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Billing ops: proposed credit + late-fee reversal for DN-4871

Grace / team / Daniel — I reviewed Ben’s impact calc and the attachment. Ops confirms we can:

- Apply a one-time credit that offsets the 9,240 duplicate tokens on invoice INV-202709-113 (credit ID CR-2027-0914-BN).
- Reverse the late fee and reopen the payment window upon BlueNova's acceptance.
- Reissue an updated invoice INV-202709-113-R with the credit applied; this will clear outstanding balance and allow ACH to go through.

I’ve created the internal ticket BILL-334 to track the backfill and billing correction. ETA to issue credit and reissue invoice after acceptance: 24 business hours.

Jonas Weber
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Harper <daniel@bluenova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Accounting <acct@bluenova.com>
Date: 2027-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Resolution proposal: credit & collection hold release for BlueNova (DN-4871)

Hi Daniel — thanks for your patience. Summary of what we found and the proposed fix: 

- Root cause: a combination of client retrying with identical request_ids plus a short-window reingestion that allowed duplicates across session boundaries (Ben’s notes attached).
- Impact: 9,240 billed tokens that are attributable to duplicate ingestion.
- Proposed remediation: one-time credit CR-2027-0914-BN for the token overage, reversal of the late fee, and reissue of invoice INV-202709-113-R. Billing ops (Jonas) will apply the credit and reissue within 24 business hours after you confirm.

Attachments included: requestids_sample.txt (sample of duplicated ids), billing_detail_export_202709.csv (billing rows), redwood_credit_proposal.pdf (credit summary + next steps).

Next steps for BlueNova: please reply with either 
  A) Accept credit and we release the collection hold so you can proceed with payment, or
  B) Request additional evidence (we’ll provide the full 3k+ row request id export and token mappings).

If you accept, we’ll take care of the invoice update and send a new payment link. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize the patch so this class of duplicates is collapsed in future.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: requestids_sample.txt, billing_detail_export_202709.csv, redwood_credit_proposal.pdf
